correctness.rationale: Under the source's global-existence hypotheses, conservation of the four nonnegative populations gives 0≤i≤N. Positivity and preservation of constants for the Neumann resolvent give 0≤b≤N. On that interval h(b)≤max(1,N^(p−1))b for p≥1 (if N≤1, simply use b^p≤b). The Neumann condition yields equal integrals of b and i, and the recovery balance bounds the space-time integral of i, so Fubini gives a finite cumulative susceptible loss coefficient a.e. The exact scalar solution then gives positive limiting susceptibility a.e. on the initially positive set. For extinction pointwise, the same recovery balance gives time-integrable i at each point. The infected time derivative is bounded on the tail by conservation, bounded coefficients and bounded incidence, including at the fixed delayed time. Nonnegative time-integrable i with bounded derivative tends to zero. Monotonicity of s and r gives their pointwise limits; the population bound gives the stated L1 conclusions by dominated convergence. The original theorem phrases positivity using an a.e.-positive initial density. The frozen localized a.e. assertion, stated explicitly, follows from its Fubini proof without requiring global initial positivity.
residual_risks: This is a mathematical proof check, not formal verification; no decay rate or conclusion for p<1 is assessed.

value.rationale: The bound closes a concrete mismatch between the domains of the published existence and long-time theorems. It preserves both extinction and positive residual susceptibility for every initially positive location up to a null set even in the omitted regime where the incidence has unbounded global ratio h(u)/u. The mathematical point is that the conserved population and the constant-preserving positive resolvent control the relevant range; it is not a numerical instance or a parameter substitution.
